sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house fast in Perrysburg, Ohio?
sections.html:
Perrysburg sellers can list through an agent, sell the house themselves, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. The city sits in Wood County, so deeds, tax bills and building permits involve county offices as well as city hall. Knowing which office handles which step keeps a sale from stalling.

  • A listing makes sense when the house is in condition for a lender's appraisal and showings.
  • A private sale works if a title company or attorney prepares the deed and settlement statement.
  • A cash offer fits inherited homes, rentals with tenants, and houses that need work.

sections.h2: What is Perrysburg's history, and how does it shape the housing?
sections.html:
Perrysburg is a Wood County city on the south bank of the Maumee River, about 12 miles southwest of Toledo. A federal survey team platted it in the summer of 1816, and it takes its name from Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry. Fort Meigs, begun in February 1813 on a bluff above the river, is the largest wooden walled fortification in North America, and two battles with the British were fought there in the War of 1812.

The town grew as a shipbuilding and trade center. It served as county seat from 1822 to 1868, and the railroad arrived in 1859. Wood County later moved its seat to Bowling Green, where courthouse construction began in November 1893. A cholera epidemic in 1854 killed more than 100 people, and the early settlement of Orleans had to move to higher ground after floods.

The area lies near the center of the Twelve Mile Square Reservation, land the Odawa ceded to the United States in 1795, and the 1817 Treaty of Fort Meigs ended their claim to this stretch of the river. The original 1816 survey covered 1.786 square miles. The city now measures 11.51 square miles by the 2010 Census count, so most houses sit on land added long after the first plat.

sections.h2: What does Census data say about Perrysburg homes and residents?
sections.html:
Perrysburg's median home value is $329,700 and its median household income is $111,643. Just under two thirds of homes are owner-occupied, so a sizeable share of the housing is rented.

sections.h2: Which employers, schools and amenities support demand in Perrysburg?
sections.html:
Perrysburg is the base for companies such as Owens-Illinois, a global glass container manufacturer, Burkett Restaurant Equipment and Universal Tube and Rollform Equipment. Levis Commons is the best-known shopping and dining center in the city.

Perrysburg Schools run a preschool, four elementary schools, an intermediate school, a junior high and Perrysburg High School. Saint Rose School and The Islamic School of Greater Toledo are the other schools in the city. The Way Public Library serves the Perrysburg area.

Among adults 25 and older, 57.6% hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and the average commute to work is 18.9 minutes.

sections.h2: Which city and county offices handle permits for a Perrysburg house?
sections.html:
The City of Perrysburg issues zoning permits, and it contracts with Wood County Building Inspection for building permits. A zoning permit must be obtained before the building permit is issued. The Planning and Zoning Division administers the city's codified ordinances from Chapter 1210 through Chapter 1460 and also handles code enforcement, Board of Zoning Appeals applications and the Historic Landmarks Commission.

The city's own answers to common questions are useful to a seller who is closing out past projects:

  • A fence needs a permit any time its height, style or location changes.
  • Every new shed needs a permit, including a shed that is not fixed to the ground. Sheds sit at least 5 feet from the property line and at least 10 feet from the house.
  • Trailers and recreational vehicles may sit in a front or side yard from April 1 through October 31, on a hard surface at least 5 feet from any lot line.
  • The city cannot survey lots. For lot lines, hire a certified surveyor.

Zoning questions go to the Planning and Zoning office at 201 W Indiana Avenue, phone 419-872-8060. For building permits, Wood County Building Inspection answers at 419-354-9190 on weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., or toll free at 866-860-4140.

Landlords have an extra duty. The city requires owners of rental property in Perrysburg to file a net profit income tax return on rental income and to report tenants who occupy and vacate their units.

sections.h2: How do deed transfer and property tax work in Wood County?
sections.html:
When a Perrysburg house sells, the deed goes to the Wood County Auditor first to move taxable ownership and then to the recorder. Ohio Revised Code 322.02 says any transfer tax a county levies is paid by the seller to the auditor at delivery of the deed, before the deed is presented to the recorder, and ORC 319.202 requires a statement of value from the buyer. The auditor's office answers at 419-354-9150 and 866-860-4140.

Property tax is collected by the Wood County Treasurer in two installments, due in February and July of each year. The county has roughly eighty taxing districts, each with its own rate, so your Perrysburg bill depends on the school district and levies at your address. A payment must be postmarked on or before the due date. After the due date, a 5 percent penalty applies for the first 10 days and 10 percent after that, under Ohio Revised Code 323.13.

Under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 you must give buyers a property disclosure form as soon as practicable, which covers items such as the water supply, the sewer system, the roof and foundation, and known defects. Exemptions exist for estate fiduciaries and for inherited houses you did not occupy in the past year.

sections.h2: When is a cash offer the practical choice in Perrysburg?
sections.html:
A cash offer is practical when time or condition matters more than the last dollar. Typical cases are an inherited house in Perrysburg that nobody wants to renovate, a rental with a tenant who is leaving, or an owner moving for work on a short schedule. The buyer pays for the house as it stands, so you do not manage contractors, showings or a lender's appraisal.

Request the offer in writing and compare it with a realistic listing outcome after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Ask who pays title and transfer charges, when the closing date falls, and what happens if the buyer finds a problem. You can decline an offer and still list the house.

faqs.q: Who issues building permits in Perrysburg?
faqs.a: Wood County Building Inspection issues building permits for Perrysburg, while the city's Planning and Zoning Division issues zoning permits first. You need the zoning permit before the building permit.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a fence in Perrysburg?
faqs.a: Yes, a permit is required anytime a fence changes in height, style or location. If you are replacing it with the same height and style in the same place, confirm with Planning and Zoning at 419-872-8060 before you start.

faqs.q: When are Wood County property taxes due?
faqs.a: February and July each year. Late payments carry a 5 percent penalty for the first 10 days and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: Do Perrysburg landlords owe city income tax on rent?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires owners of rental property to file a net profit income tax return for rental income from property in Perrysburg, and to report details on tenants who move in or out.

faqs.q: What do I have to disclose when I sell in Perrysburg?
faqs.a: Ohio law applies statewide, so you complete the residential property disclosure form under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 and deliver it to buyers as soon as practicable. It covers the water supply, sewer system, structure, hazardous materials and known defects.
